title: Routers & Modular Project Structure
summary: Organize code with APIRouter, prefixes, tags, and a professional project layout.

sections.content: APIRouter lets you split routes into modules. Use prefix for path grouping and tags for docs organization.

# routers/items.py
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends

router = APIRouter(
    prefix="/items",
    tags=["items"],
    dependencies=[Depends(verify_token)],  # all routes require auth
    responses={404: {"description": "Not found"}},
)

@router.get("/")
def list_items(): ...

@router.get("/{item_id}")
def get_item(item_id: int): ...

# main.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
from routers import items, users

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(items.router)
app.include_router(users.router)
prefix adds a path prefix to every route. tags group them in the docs. The route / in the router becomes /items/.

app/
├── main.py              # creates app, includes routers, lifespan
├── config.py            # Settings (pydantic-settings)
├── database.py          # engine, session, Base, get_db
├── models/              # SQLAlchemy models
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── user.py
│   └── item.py
├── schemas/             # Pydantic models (in/out)
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── user.py
│   └── item.py
├── routers/             # API endpoints per resource
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── users.py
│   └── items.py
├── crud/                # (optional) DB access functions
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── user.py
├── core/                # security, deps, exceptions
│   ├── security.py
│   └── deps.py
└── tests/
    ├── conftest.py
    └── test_users.py

sections.title: Key rules
sections.content: 1) Schemas (Pydantic) ≠ Models (SQLAlchemy) — never return ORM objects directly without a response model. 2) Routers stay thin: parse → call service/crud → respond. 3) Business logic lives in crud/ or services/, not in endpoints.

code_challenge.description: Create a FastAPI app with two routers: items (prefix=/items) and users (prefix=/users). Each has a GET / route returning {"resource": "name"}.

quiz.question: What does APIRouter prefix do?
options: Adds a path prefix to every route in the router
Adds a tag in the docs
quiz.explanation: prefix='/items' means every route in the router is prefixed with /items. A @router.get('/') route becomes GET /items/.

quiz.question: How do you include a router in the app?
quiz.explanation: Use app.include_router(router) to register an APIRouter. You can also add prefix= or tags= at include time.

quiz.question: What is the difference between schemas and models?
options: Schemas are Pydantic (validation/serialization), models are SQLAlchemy (database)
Schemas are for requests, models for responses
Models are Pydantic, schemas are SQLAlchemy
quiz.explanation: Schemas (Pydantic BaseModel) handle request validation and response serialization. Models (SQLAlchemy) represent database tables. Never return ORM objects without a response_model schema.

quiz.question: Where should business logic live in a modular FastAPI app?
quiz.explanation: Routers should stay thin: parse request → call service/crud → respond. Business logic belongs in crud/ or a services/ layer, keeping routes testable and clean.

quiz.question: What does the tags parameter do in APIRouter?
options: Groups routes in the Swagger/ReDoc docs
quiz.explanation: tags=['items'] groups all routes under an 'items' section in the auto-generated docs (Swagger UI and ReDoc), making the API documentation organized.
